claims.text: What the image looks like RUQ / LUQ views: assess above the diaphragm for hemothorax (anechoic above bright diaphragm)
claims.quote: Also assess above diaphragm for hemothorax (anechoic above bright diaphragm).

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Sensitivity: for hemothorax, US can detect as little as ~20 mL of pleural fluid
claims.quote: For hemothorax: US can detect as little as ~20 mL of pleural fluid.
claims.locator: FAST & eFAST Exam, Indications, Probe, Sequence, Performance

claims.text: Sus from Sx and physical findings; dx = typically confirmed by chest radiograph and sometimes E-FAST or CT
claims.quote: Hemothorax is suspected based on symptoms and physical findings. Diagnosis is typically confirmed by chest radiograph and sometimes E-FAST or CT.

claims.text: Eti USU laceration of the lung, an IC vessel or an internal mammary a.; great-vessel inj (eg, aorta, SVC) can also cause it but = typically rapidly lethal. From penetrating or blunt thoracic trauma, often w pneumothorax (hemopneumothorax)
claims.quote: The usual cause of hemothorax is laceration of the lung, intercostal vessel, or an internal mammary artery. Injury to the great vessels (eg, aorta, superior vena cava) can also cause hemothorax but it is typically rapidly lethal. Hemothorax can result from penetrating or blunt thoracic trauma and is often accompanied by pneumothorax (hemopneumothorax).

claims.text: Massive hemothorax = most often defined as rapid accum of ≥ 1500 mL of blood; shock = common
claims.quote: Hemorrhage volume ranges from minimal to massive. Massive hemothorax is most often defined as rapid accumulation of ≥ 1500 mL of blood (1). Shock is common.

claims.text: Sx Lrg volumes: often dyspnea, ↓breath sounds and dullness to percussion (often hard to appreciate during initial eval of multi injuries); findings may be unremarkable w smaller hemothoraces
claims.quote: Patients with large hemorrhage volume are often dyspneic and have decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion (often difficult to appreciate during initial evaluation of patients with multiple injuries). Findings may be unremarkable in patients with smaller hemothoraces.

claims.text: Tx and next step Signs of hypovolemia (eg, tachy, hypotension): IV crystalloid and sometimes blood transfusion
claims.quote: Patients with signs of hypovolemia (eg, tachycardia, hypotension) are given IV crystalloid and sometimes blood transfusion (see Intravenous Fluid Resuscitation).

claims.text: If visible on chest radiograph (USU ≈ 500 mL) or w pneumothorax: chest tube (pigtail [14 Fr] or lrger bore [28 to 32 Fr]) in the fifth or sixth intercostal space, midaxillary line; drainage improves ventilation, decreases the risk of clotted hemothorax (empyema or fibrothorax) and helps assess ongoing blood loss
claims.quote: If blood volume is sufficient to be visible on chest radiograph (usually requiring approximately 500 mL), or if pneumothorax is present, a chest tube (pigtail [14 French] or larger bore [28 to 32 French]) is inserted in the fifth or sixth intercostal space in the midaxillary line (1). Tube drainage improves ventilation, decreases risk of clotted hemothorax (which can lead to empyema or fibrothorax), and facilitates assessment of ongoing blood loss and diaphragmatic integrity.

claims.text: Urgent thoracotomy: initial bleed > 1500 mL, or bleed > 200 mL/hr for > 2 to 4 hrs w resp or hemodynamic compromise or a need for repeated blood transfusions
claims.quote: Urgent thoracotomy is indicated in either of the following situations (2): Initial bleeding is >1500 mL Bleeding is > 200 mL/hour for > 2 to 4 hours and causes respiratory or hemodynamic compromise or the need for repeated blood transfusions.
